links.outcome: Reproducibility of answers when identical prompts were resubmitted 24 hours apart
links.effect: ChatGPT 3.5 showed a 7.5% accuracy decline on repeat testing; some models gave different antimicrobial recommendations for the same case; Microsoft Copilot was most stable.
links.quote: AI-generated responses were found to change over time, with some models giving different antimicrobial recommendations for the same case scenario upon repeated testing.

links.outcome: Accuracy of antimicrobial selection and dosing recommendations
links.effect: Therapy-related questions had the lowest accuracy (57.1%); ChatGPT 3.5 antimicrobial treatment accuracy was 56.6%; Perplexity AI and Meta AI showed variability in drug selection and dosing adjustments.
links.quote: AI platforms offer potential in infectious disease education but demonstrate limitations in pharmacotherapy decision-making, particularly in antimicrobial selection and dosing accuracy.

screen.reason: Evaluates the accuracy and consistency of several commercial LLMs on textbook multiple-choice questions in infectious disease.
